title: Sion Boundary Counterexample
body_html:
Sion Boundary Counterexample

Let $S=T=[0,1]$ and define $f:S\times T\to\{0,-1\}$ by $$ f(s,t)= \begin{cases} -1, & t=0\text{ and }s<1/2,\\ -1, & t=1\text{ and }s\ge 1/2,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} $$ This game has no value in pure strategies, while Sion's hypotheses fail only at the boundary point $t=1$.

The pure quantities are $$ \sup_s\inf_t f(s,t)=-1,\qquad \inf_t\sup_s f(s,t)=0. $$ Nevertheless, the mixed extension does have a value, equal to $-1/2$. Player 1 can guarantee this by playing uniformly on $[0,1]$, or by mixing equally between $0$ and $1$.
